pr_body:
Fixes #31256

We want to run the FileSystem unit tests in .NET Framework again. This PR helps enable the supported tests in that .NET version and skips the ones testing new features.

I split my PR into one commit per modified file, to make the review easier.

[Original PR](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/32953) - _I forced pushed to this branch while the PR was closed, which prevented me from reopening it._
pr_comments:
I had a conversation with @ericstj about this. In short, this change is not seen as critical or needed so we have decided to close it.

Having .NET Framework unit tests enabled is useful and valuable when we are porting new code or when we are writing new tests for existing code. Currently we don't have any APIs that need to be ported, and most of the changes we introduce in this namespace are either new APIs or bug fixes.
It's more valuable to have the differences between APIs in our documentation, so I'll do a pass on these unit tests and ensure we have the differences documented in MS Docs.

issue_context.body:
Per https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/pull/41452#issuecomment-544650139

If instead we decide to close this issue, please delete the netfx-specific tests added in the above PR.
comments: Triage: We definitely want to do this to make sure we're catching unintentional regressions and document where we intentionally change behavior from .NET Framework.

Per [this comment](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/33063#issuecomment-617416082), we won't be re-enabling the tests for .NET Framework.
We would still have to submit a PR to remove the Framework specific tests from FileSystem.

> We definitely want to do this to make sure we're catching unintentional regressions and document where we intentionally change behavior from .NET Framework.

Just to address this: our existing tests should cover this.  When we make a change to a test case we should note that it corresponds to a behavior change that's may be a breaking change.  We don't need to run the tests against .NETFramework in order to catch that.

If we do decide to write new tests that cover API that exists on .NETFramework it would make sense for the initial author of those tests to run them against .NETFramework to understand their differences.

review_comments: This is talking about a colon.  The InlineData is using a bar, not a colon.  Is this a copy/paste error, or am I misreading it?

The comment does not belong here. Copy/paste error. I'll remove it.

I copied the `PathsWithInvalidColons_ThrowIOException_Core`method to test the pipe character separately.

I had to remove the string with a pipe from the list in TestData.cs because it was the only case that was failing differently in Framework (`ArgumentException`).

The `EncryptDecrypt_NotSupported` test method is failing with a different exception than the expected one. I'm investigating:

```
Expected: typeof(System.PlatformNotSupportedException)
Actual:   typeof(System.IO.FileNotFoundException): Could not find file 'C:\h\w\AB0D0973\w\A7620956\e\path'.
      ---- System.IO.FileNotFoundException : Could not find file 'C:\h\w\AB0D0973\w\A7620956\e\path'.
Stack Trace:
    at System.IO.__Error.WinIOError(Int32 errorCode, String maybeFullPath)
    at System.IO.File.Encrypt(String path)
```

```csharp
        [SkipOnTargetFramework(TargetFrameworkMonikers.Netcoreapp)]
        [Fact]
        public static void EncryptDecrypt_NotSupported()
        {
            Assert.Throws<PlatformNotSupportedException>(() => File.Encrypt("path"));
            Assert.Throws<PlatformNotSupportedException>(() => File.Decrypt("path"));
        }

```

Seems that we are succeeding in calling the .NET Framework P/Invoke and encryption is supported by the underlying OS where the test is being executed, but since the path does not exist, we throw the exception message.

We were expecting to reach one of the lines that throw `PlatformNotSupportedException`:

https://referencesource.microsoft.com/#mscorlib/system/io/file.cs,324 // PAL + Not NT
https://referencesource.microsoft.com/#mscorlib/system/io/file.cs,338 // Not NTFS

But instead we now throw because the path does not exist.

I'll update this test and remove the `SkipOnTargetFramework` attribute. I suspect both .NET Framework and .NET Core would support executing the method and would throw `FileNotFoundException`.
This is only needed as Framework can't handle deleting the special names without prepending the `\\?\`
I wouldn't remove it, just add a comment for future generations to understand why it is here.
Why is this one written this way, and the test change a page above is using the Throws that takes two generic arguments?

Because of the `ThrowsAny`. The unit tests that use `ThrowsAny` can throw any exception that inherits from `IOException`.

There are some test classes in `FileSystem` that inherit from others, and the APIs are tested in a very similar way. The only thing that changes is the type of exception expected (for example `DirectoryNotFoundException` vs `FileNotFoundException`).

It took me some time to figure out why when I tried to use `Throws<IOException>` was not working for all cases. It was because of the test class inheritance.

Would it help if I add a comment above the test class to explain this?
Same question about when we choose to use which structure for this kind of test.
Same question.  Is there a reason they need to be different?  If not, let's try to be consistent.  Thanks.
